data.name: Divyani
data.gender_notes: Divyani is used as a unisex name in Hindu naming traditions.
data.long_meaning: Divyani is derived from the Sanskrit word ‘Divy’, meaning divine, and ‘Ani’, meaning one or unique. This name is bestowed upon a child believed to be a divine and unique presence in the world. The name Divyani carries the meaning “Divine, Celestial, Radiant” and is chosen by families in Hindu traditions for the positive qualities it expresses. Linguistically it belongs to the Sanskrit tradition and is also used in Hindi, Sanskrit, Marathi. Parents who choose Divyani usually hope their child will grow to embody divine, celestial, radiant and live with faith, good character and purpose.
data.spiritual_meaning: Represents the inner divine light that illuminates the soul.
data.etymology: Divyani belongs to the Sanskrit linguistic tradition and is used in Hindu naming. Its recorded meaning is “Divine, Celestial, Radiant.”
data.numerology_meaning: In Pythagorean numerology the letters of Divyani total 3, giving a life-path number of 3. Number 3 is linked with Jupiter and with the qualities of creativity, expression and optimism.

historical_references.reference: Divyani was an important goddess in the Shakta tradition of Hinduism. She was believed to be the goddess of knowledge, wisdom, and learning. Her name is derived from the Sanskrit word 'divya' which means 'divine'. In the Puranic texts, she is described as the daughter of Lord Shiva and Goddess Parvati.
historical_references.context: The Shakta tradition of Hinduism emerged in the third to fifth century CE, with a focus on the goddess Shakti and her various forms. Divyani, as a goddess of knowledge and wisdom, would have been an important deity in this tradition.

historical_references.reference: Divyani is also identified with Saraswati, the goddess of knowledge and learning in Hinduism. According to some legends, Divyani was born from the tears of Goddess Saraswati when she wept over the loss of her husband, Lord Brahma. This association further solidified her role as a goddess of knowledge and wisdom.
historical_references.context: The association of Divyani with Saraswati is mentioned in various Hindu texts and legends, but the exact time period of this belief is unknown.
